The salary range is from $80,000 to $85,000 per year plus super. 

Primary responsibilities Machinist
•     Operate machine tools such as lathes, milling machines,
•     Manufacture rods, glands, pistons, barrels, bases, fittings, bushes
•     Review specifications for a job.
•     Calculate where to cut or bore.
•     Shape steel, aluminium, other materials.
•     Determine how fast or slow workpiece is fed into machine.
•     Determine how much material to remove.
•     Select tools and materials for the job.
•     Plan the sequence of cutting and finishing operations.
•     Mark the workpiece to show where cuts should be made.
•     Position workpiece on the lathe or milling machine.
•     Monitor and control feed rate and speed.
•     Ensure workpiece is properly lubricated and/or cooled.
•     Regulate temperature of workpiece.
•     Detect problems by listening for specific sounds.
•     Adjust cutting speed to compensate for harmonic vibrations.
•     Monitor the accuracy of cuts.
•     Replace dull cutting tools.
•     Check accuracy of work against specifications.
•     Ability to use precision tools (eg. Micrometers internal & external)
•     Use manual machinery.

Primary responsibilities Fitter
 
•     Takes the components assemble together, barrel, rod, piston and gland, assemble, to make a complete cylinder
•     Seal assembly
•     Then test cylinder, make sure has no leaks, by- pass pressure test, close it up, plug and press in the bushes
•     Record the testing
•     ID cylinder with job number
•     Completed cylinder for spraying
•     Torque nuts and bolts to right specifications
•     Press the bushes

Qualifications/Knowledge/Skills/Experience
 
•     Certificate Ill in Engineering - Mechanical Trade (Fitter & Machinist)
•     Good mechanical aptitude.
•     Excellent reading comprehension
•     Physical Stamina

result.description:
Who We Are
We're a proud Tasmanian family-owned business with over a century of experience in general engineering. Our modern fabrication and machining workshops are located just 10 minutes south of Hobart in Kingston. We specialise in the manufacture, repair, refurbishment, installation, and maintenance of industrial equipment.

The Opportunity
We're on the lookout for skilled Boilermaker Welders to join our dynamic team. Our workshop operations cover a wide range of fabrication and welding tasks, from light to heavy work with steel, stainless steel and aluminium components. You'll work from engineering drawings and use equipment such as CNC plasma cutters, plate rolls, brake presses, bandsaws, and various welding techniques such as MIG, TIG and stick.

What You'll Do
Operate equipment such as plate rolls, rotators, bandsaws, presses and overhead cranes.
Use a variety of welding equipment including MIG, TIG, and stick.
Fabricate steel, aluminium, and stainless-steel components and assemblies.
Carryout repairs on plant and equipment.
Perform welding tasks that range from basic general-purpose applications to coded welding on quality-critical components and equipment.

Why Join Us?
At Saunders & Ward, we offer:
The option to work a 4-day week.
Excellent working conditions.
Stable employment with a well-established, family-owned company.
A diverse range of stimulating work.
Modern, well-organised and clean workshops.
A friendly, safety-focused culture.
Regular overtime.
A graded pay structure that rewards skills and experience.
Annual performance and wage reviews.
Rostered days off (RDOs).

What We're Looking For
To be successful in this role, you should have:
A strong commitment to safe work practices.
A fabrication trade qualification.
Engineering workshop experience.
Experience with mild steel MIG welding and fabrication.
The ability to complete jobs on time and to quality standards.
The ability to pass drug and alcohol screening.

If you're ready to bring your skills and experience to a great team, we'd love to hear from you! Please submit your cover letter and resume to our Fabrication Manager, Matt Brown, via our online application.
